description: WS-TRNX-TABLE AT ITS LAST ELEMENT - the upper bound of a 1-based table, which gate G33 requires be asserted at both ends: case07 owns the first element and this case owns the last. The correspondence is stated explicitly rather than left implied (practice B8): COBOL WS-CARD-NUM (51) is Java index [50], COBOL WS-TRAN-NUM (51, 10) and WS-TRAN-REST (51, 10) are Java [50][9], and WS-TRCT (51) is Java [50]. THE SUBJECT'S SHAPE: app/cbl/CBSTM03A.CBL:L225-L233 declares 01 WS-TRNX-TABLE as 05 WS-CARD-TBL OCCURS 51 TIMES holding 10 WS-CARD-NUM PIC X(16) and 10 WS-TRAN-TBL OCCURS 10 TIMES holding 15 WS-TRAN-NUM PIC X(16) and 15 WS-TRAN-REST PIC X(318), and it declares SEPARATELY 01 WS-TRN-TBL-CNTR as 05 WS-TRN-TBL-CTR OCCURS 51 TIMES holding 10 WS-TRCT PIC S9(4) COMP. The counter array stays a parallel OCCURS 51 in its own 01 item rather than being merged into the table for tidiness (practice B5). The geometry is arithmetic from the PICTURE clauses, not an estimate (practice B11): one card slot is 16 + 10 x (16 + 318) = 16 + 3,340 = 3,356 bytes, so the whole table is 51 x 3,356 = 171,156 bytes, and WS-TRAN-REST X(318) is exactly the width of app/cpy/COSTM01.CPY's TRNX-REST - the table stores the record minus its 16-byte card number, which is held once per slot in WS-CARD-NUM rather than ten times. WHY 51 IS THE HIGHEST SUBSCRIPT AND WHAT WOULD MISS IT: COBOL subscripts run from 1 to the declared OCCURS inclusive, so WS-CARD-NUM (51) and WS-TRAN-NUM (51, 10) are the last valid elements of the two dimensions. A translation that allocated 51 elements and then addressed [51] would run past the end, and one that iterated an index from 1 while testing < 51 would silently drop the fifty-first card - the statement for the highest card would come out with no transaction line and a zero total instead of ten lines and 550.55. This case therefore pins the boundary VALUES and not merely a count. HOW THE BOUNDARY IS REACHED: 8100-TRNXFILE-OPEN reads the first row and primes the subscripts - MOVE TRNX-CARD-NUM TO WS-SAVE-CARD, MOVE 1 TO CR-CNT, MOVE 0 TO TR-CNT (:L757-L759). 8500-READTRNX-READ then tests the saved card at :L819: the same card takes ADD 1 TO TR-CNT, a new card takes MOVE TR-CNT TO WS-TRCT (CR-CNT), ADD 1 TO CR-CNT, MOVE 1 TO TR-CNT (:L822-L824), and the three stores at :L827-L829 then address WS-CARD-NUM (CR-CNT), WS-TRAN-NUM (CR-CNT, TR-CNT) and WS-TRAN-REST (CR-CNT, TR-CNT). Reaching CR-CNT = 51 therefore takes 51 DISTINCT card numbers, and reaching TR-CNT = 10 on that fifty-first card takes ten rows sharing it. The '10' arm at :L841 leaves the loop on end of file and 8599-EXIT's MOVE TR-CNT TO WS-TRCT (CR-CNT) at :L850 writes the last group's count, which is what makes WS-TRCT (51) = 10 rather than 0 - the store for a card group happens at the break AFTER it, so the final group is closed only here. THE SEED, AND THE ONE COMPOSED CARD THAT IS UNAVOIDABLE: the table holds 51 cards while app/data/ASCII/cardxref.txt holds 50 rows, so exactly one card in the seed cannot be a cross-reference card. It is placed at slot 1 as 0100000000000000, below every real card, because that is the only arrangement in which the fifty real cards occupy slots 2 through 51 in cross-reference order AND the boundary slot 51 holds a card a cross-reference read can still reach - a card above them all would fill slot 51 but could never be looked up. Its own transaction is loaded and never emitted, since 4000-TRNXFILE-GET only writes a card the cross-reference names. Slots 2 through 50 carry the first 49 cardxref cards, one transaction each, and each of those rows is real fixture data rather than invented (practice B1): it is that card's dailytran.txt row with the lowest DALYTRAN-ID, put through STEP010's own projection OUTREC FIELDS=(1:263,16,17:1,262,279:279,50) (app/jcl/CREASTMT.JCL:L54), which moves the 16-byte card number from offset 263 to the front, follows it with the 262 bytes from DALYTRAN-ID through DALYTRAN-MERCHANT-ZIP and copies 50 bytes from 279 - so TRNX-ORIG-TS arrives whole and TRNX-PROC-TS, blank in the source rows, arrives blank. CVTRA06Y and CVTRA05Y share every width and offset, so the positions the SORT names land on the same spans, and the same projection reproduces case07's row from dailytran.txt row 20 exactly. Slot 51 is card 9805583408996588 - cardxref.txt row 50's XREF-CARD-NUM, and the highest card in that ascending fixture - with TEN rows. Those ten are composed field by field from COSTM01.CPY rather than projected, because no fixture can supply them: dailytran.txt holds exactly six rows for each of its fifty cards, so a tenth transaction for any one card does not exist to be derived. Each composed TRNX-ID encodes the subscript pair it occupies - 51 followed by ten zeros followed by the four-digit TR-JMP - so WS-TRAN-NUM (51, 1) is 5100000000000001 and WS-TRAN-NUM (51, 10) is 5100000000000010, and each TRNX-DESC names the same subscript in words. The ten amounts are 10.01, 20.02, 30.03, 40.04, 50.05, 60.06, 70.07, 80.08, 90.09 and 100.10, which sum to exactly 550.55 - the value ADD TRNX-AMT TO WS-TOTAL-AMT (:L429) accumulates and ST-TOTAL-TRAMT reports, so a dropped or duplicated element changes the total line as well as the detail lines. Every seeded row is exactly 350 bytes: TRNX-KEY's 16 + 16 composite key, corroborated by DELDEF01's KEYS(32 0) and RECORDSIZE(350 350) at app/jcl/CREASTMT.JCL:L30 and :L32, then TRNX-REST's 318, whose trailing FILLER X(20) is emitted as spaces - which the declared total width proves (gate G21). SORT ORDER IS MANDATORY, NOT COSMETIC: SORT FIELDS=(263,16,CH,A,1,16,CH,A) at app/jcl/CREASTMT.JCL:L53 delivers TRNXFILE ascending by TRNX-CARD-NUM then TRNX-ID, so the seed is in that order - 51 cards ascending, and the boundary card's ten rows ascending by id. Two separate mechanisms depend on it. The card-break test at :L819 only groups a card into ONE slot if its rows are contiguous, so out-of-order rows would split a card across slots and change every subscript above it. And the early exit at :L419, WS-CARD-NUM (CR-JMP) > XREF-CARD-NUM, abandons the scan the moment the table's card sorts past the wanted one, which is correct only because both sequences ascend. THE CONSUMING SIDE, AND WHAT IT PROVES AT THE TOP OF THE TABLE: XREFFILE is seeded with cardxref.txt rows 48, 49 and 50 (zero-based fromRow 47, rowCount 3), whose cards are 9501733721429893, 9680294154603697 and 9805583408996588 - table slots 49, 50 and 51 - so the run walks the last three slots and finishes on the last element. 1000-MAINLINE re-primes MOVE 1 TO CR-JMP and MOVE ZERO TO WS-TOTAL-AMT per customer (:L324-L325). For the first two the outer PERFORM VARYING at :L417-L419 matches at CR-JMP = 49 and CR-JMP = 50 and then stops because the next slot's card sorts higher; each inner loop at :L422-L423 runs TR-JMP = 1 only, since WS-TRCT is 1 for those slots. For the boundary card no table card sorts higher, so the scan runs to CR-JMP = 51, matches, and the inner loop runs TR-JMP = 1 through 10 INCLUSIVE and terminates when TR-JMP becomes 11 - both ends are visible in the pinned records, as the detail line for 5100000000000001 at 10.01 and the detail line for 5100000000000010 at 100.10. The outer loop then increments CR-JMP to 52 and leaves on CR-JMP > CR-CNT; the UNTIL condition's OR is evaluated left to right, so WS-CARD-NUM (52) is never evaluated, and reversing those two operands would read past the table on this very case. NO OVERFLOW IS PROBED, DELIBERATELY: there is no fifty-second card anywhere in this seed and no expectation about one. CBSTM03A neither tests CR-CNT against 51 nor handles overflow, so a fifty-second card has no defined behaviour to assert; pinning one would invent semantics the source does not have (practices B5 and B1). The capacity is an inherited constraint of the legacy design and is recorded as one. UNIT AND INVOCATION: statement.StatementGenerationJobA as a BATCH_JOB, reached at step/Tasklet level with statement.StatementGenerationJobB as its constructor-injected collaborator - no JobLauncher, no job repository and no HTTP anywhere in the path (gate G51). jobParameters is empty because no step of app/jcl/CREASTMT.JCL carries a PARM; the only PARM in this estate is INTCALC.jcl's. Every call reports '00', no abend arm is reached, and expectedReturnCode is 0. WIDTHS AND COUNTS: STMTFILE records are exactly 80 bytes - FD-STMTFILE-REC PIC X(80) at app/cbl/CBSTM03A.CBL:L45 and DCB=(LRECL=80,BLKSIZE=8000,RECFM=FB) at app/jcl/CREASTMT.JCL:L89 - and HTMLFILE records are exactly 100 - FD-HTMLFILE-REC PIC X(100) at :L47 and DCB=(LRECL=100,BLKSIZE=800,RECFM=FB) at CREASTMT.JCL:L94, which supersedes the LRECL=80 of :L69 because that DD belongs to STEP030's pre-delete and this one to the creating step (risk R-G). CREASTMT.JCL:L90 is corrupted in the source and is cited around rather than repaired: its ' 00,RECFM=FB)' remnant reads like an LRECL=100 for STMTFILE and is not one, and app/jcl is read-only (practices B4 and B3). Per statement the text stream is 19 + N records - 16 from 5000-CREATE-STATEMENT (:L460 and :L488-L502), N detail lines from 6000-WRITE-TRANS and 3 closing records at :L435-L437 - and the HTML stream is 64 + 11N: 22 from 5100-WRITE-HTML-HEADER, 34 from 5200-WRITE-HTML-NMADBS, 11 per transaction and 8 closing records at :L439-L454. This run produces three statements at N = 1, N = 1 and N = 10, so STMTFILE is 20 + 20 + 29 = 69 records and HTMLFILE is 75 + 75 + 174 = 324, which is the 393 records pinned below and the two rowCount values declared in expectedDatasets. Every record is pinned individually and the differ compares in both directions, so an extra record is a difference as surely as a wrong one. CROSS-REFERENCE ROWS STAY 36 BYTES: cardxref.txt is 36 bytes per record where CVACT03Y declares 50, because the fixture omits the trailing FILLER X(14). The seed keeps the fixture bytes verbatim and CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD_36_TO_50 is the single owner of the pad (gate G16), so no case pads by hand. XREF-CUST-ID and XREF-ACCT-ID of the three rows drive the keyed reads at 2000-CUSTFILE-GET and 3000-ACCTFILE-GET, which is why the three statements are for customers 000000009, 000000001 and 000000040 against accounts 00000000009, 00000000001 and 00000000040 - the third being Davon Demond Emmerich at ACCT-CURR-BAL 43.00 with FICO 284, and not any master file's first row. PROVENANCE AND DETERMINISM: every expected value here is STATICALLY DERIVED - read out of app/cbl/CBSTM03A.CBL's write paragraphs, the copybook offsets of COSTM01.CPY, CVACT03Y.cpy, CVACT01Y.cpy and CUSTREC.cpy, the DD contracts of CREASTMT.JCL and the three ASCII fixtures - and NEVER captured from a live COBOL execution, which AAP 0.7.6 proves impossible in this environment across eight verified blockers (risk R-A, practice B12). All text is US-ASCII, the code page the nine fixtures are written in and the one the harness names explicitly (practice B8). Nothing here reads a clock: the timestamps in the composed rows are fixed literals in the seed and no expectation depends on the time of the run (practice B7). Gates: G33 primarily, with G15, G16, G18, G19, G20, G21 and G51. WHAT THE RUN LEAVES BEHIND, OBSERVED RATHER THAN ASKED ABOUT: app/jcl/CREASTMT.JCL:L87-L96 declares both outputs DISP=(NEW,CATLG,DELETE), so a run that reaches 9999-GOBACK retains exactly the records it wrote and a run that does not retains none of them. Both datasets are opened on every path that runs at all, which makes both observable on every such path, so this case declares a FINAL_STATE expectation for each - byte for byte, and identical to its WRITES channel because this run completes with RETURN-CODE 0. It is declared unconditionally rather than only for the cases whose adapter chose to look: an observation selected by consulting the expectation makes the two sides of the comparison one side, and a case that ought to have pinned a retained record but did not would have had nothing observed to contradict it.
